Tomato_Early_blight.symptoms: Brown circular spots with concentric yellow rings on older leaves. Infected leaves turn yellow and drop early, reducing photosynthesis.
Tomato_Early_blight.treatment: Spray Mancozeb 2g per litre every 7 days.
Tomato_Early_blight.prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation. Remove and destroy infected leaves. Use mulching to prevent soil splash.
Tomato_Early_blight.advice: Practice 2-3 year crop rotation. Manage irrigation to reduce humidity around foliage. Balance fertilizer applications.
Tomato_Early_blight.immediate_action: Remove all visibly infected leaves immediately. Do not compost them — burn or bury away from the field. Begin fungicide spray within 24 hours.
Tomato_Early_blight.chemical_treatment: Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2g/litre water, spray every 7 days. Alternatively, Chlorothalonil 75 WP @ 2g/litre. Rotate between fungicides to prevent resistance.
Tomato_Early_blight.organic_alternative: Spray neem oil solution (5ml/litre) every 5 days. Apply copper-based bordeaux mixture (1%) as preventive spray. Use Trichoderma viride bio-fungicide.
Tomato_Early_blight.farmer_tips:
1. Water at the base of plants, never overhead.
2. Space plants 45-60cm apart for good airflow.
3. Apply balanced NPK fertilizer — excess nitrogen worsens blight.
4. Scout fields twice a week during humid weather.
5. Stake tomatoes to keep foliage off the ground.

Tomato_Late_blight.symptoms: Dark water-soaked patches on leaves and stems that spread rapidly. White mold visible under leaves in humid conditions. Fruits develop firm brown rot.
Tomato_Late_blight.prevention: Ensure proper plant spacing and reduce canopy humidity. Avoid working in wet fields.
Tomato_Late_blight.advice: Late blight spreads extremely fast. Act within 24 hours of first symptoms. Remove and destroy infected plants entirely.
Tomato_Late_blight.immediate_action: URGENT: Remove and burn all infected plants immediately — do not delay. Spray the entire field with systemic fungicide within 24 hours. Alert neighboring farmers.
Tomato_Late_blight.chemical_treatment: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold) @ 2.5g/litre, spray every 5-7 days. Also use Cymoxanil + Mancozeb as alternating spray. Cover undersides of leaves thoroughly.
Tomato_Late_blight.organic_alternative: Spray copper hydroxide (3g/litre) every 5 days as preventive treatment. Potassium bicarbonate spray (5g/litre) may help slow spread. Biological control with Bacillus subtilis (Serenade).
Tomato_Late_blight.farmer_tips:
1. Late blight can destroy entire fields in 3-5 days in wet weather — act immediately.
2. Increase plant spacing to at least 60cm.
3. Never leave infected crop debris in the field.
4. Avoid planting in the same field for 2-3 seasons.
5. Plant resistant varieties (e.g., Arka Rakshak) in future seasons.

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark water-soaked lesions with yellow halo on leaves and fruits. Spots may enlarge and merge. Severely infected leaves drop early.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.treatment: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP or Streptocycline 200ppm.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds. Avoid work in wet fields to prevent spread.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.advice: Bacterial diseases spread through rain splash and tools. Sanitize pruning tools with bleach solution regularly.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.immediate_action: Stop all overhead irrigation immediately. Remove heavily infected leaves. Spray bactericide the same day symptoms are noticed.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.chemical_treatment: Copper Oxychloride 50 WP @ 3g/litre, spray every 7-10 days. Streptocycline @ 200ppm (0.2g/litre) combined with Copper fungicide. Avoid copper resistance by rotating bactericides.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.organic_alternative: Spray diluted copper soap (neem oil + copper) solution. Apply compost tea to boost plant immunity. Use disease-free certified seeds from reputable sources.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.farmer_tips:
1. Use drip irrigation instead of sprinklers — wet foliage spreads bacteria.
2. Dip seeds in hot water (50°C for 25 minutes) before planting to kill seed-borne bacteria.
3. Disinfect farm tools with 10% bleach solution daily.
4. Remove and burn infected plants from the field.
5. Avoid working in the field when plants are wet.

Tomato_healthy.symptoms: Leaves are deep green, firm, and free from any spots or discoloration. Plant shows vigorous growth.
Tomato_healthy.prevention: Maintain balanced fertilization and regular monitoring.
Tomato_healthy.advice: Maintain consistent irrigation and monitor weekly for any early pest signs.
Tomato_healthy.immediate_action: No immediate action needed. Continue regular maintenance routine.
Tomato_healthy.chemical_treatment: No chemical treatment required. Your crop is healthy.
Tomato_healthy.organic_alternative: Apply vermicompost or compost to maintain soil health. Spray neem oil (preventive) once a month during high humidity periods.
Tomato_healthy.farmer_tips:
1. Water deeply 2-3 times per week rather than shallow daily watering.
2. Apply balanced NPK fertilizer every 3 weeks.
3. Inspect leaves (top and bottom) every week for early signs of pests or disease.
4. Stake plants properly to improve airflow and reduce disease risk.
5. Maintain a clean field — remove fallen leaves and debris regularly.

Potato_Early_blight.symptoms: Brown circular spots with concentric target-like rings on older leaves. Infected tissue yellows around spots. Severe infection reduces tuber size.
Potato_Early_blight.treatment: Spray Chlorothalonil 75 WP or Mancozeb 75 WP every 7-10 days.
Potato_Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops. Avoid water stress. Use certified seed tubers.
Potato_Early_blight.advice: Early blight is most severe when plants are under nutrient stress. Ensure adequate potassium nutrition for stronger plant resistance.
Potato_Early_blight.immediate_action: Apply fungicide spray immediately at first sign of target-like spots. Remove infected lower leaves and dispose away from field.
Potato_Early_blight.chemical_treatment: Chlorothalonil 75 WP @ 2g/litre or Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5g/litre, every 7-10 days. Azoxystrobin 23 SC @ 1ml/litre for systemic control. Alternate between products.
Potato_Early_blight.organic_alternative: Neem oil spray (5ml/litre) every 5-7 days. Apply compost and potassium-rich organic manure to build plant resistance. Bordeaux mixture (1%) as preventive spray.
Potato_Early_blight.farmer_tips:
1. Use certified disease-free seed tubers only.
2. Avoid planting potato in the same field for 2-3 years.
3. Ensure adequate potassium — it builds resistance to blight.
4. Avoid overhead irrigation in the evening — wet leaves overnight invite fungal growth.
5. Hill soil around plants to protect tubers from infection.

Potato_Late_blight.symptoms: Dark water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems spreading rapidly. Purple-brown patches appear on leaves, white mold under leaves in humid weather. Tubers show reddish-brown rot.
Potato_Late_blight.treatment: Apply Metalaxyl + Mancozeb or Cymoxanil fungicide immediately.
Potato_Late_blight.prevention: Use certified seed. Destroy infected plant debris. Avoid excessive irrigation.
Potato_Late_blight.advice: This is the same disease that caused the Irish Potato Famine. It can destroy an entire field in 5-7 days. Immediate action is essential.
Potato_Late_blight.immediate_action: EMERGENCY: Begin fungicide application today. Remove and burn heavily infected plants. Reduce irrigation immediately. Harvest mature tubers early if blight is severe.
Potato_Late_blight.chemical_treatment: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil) @ 2.5g/litre every 5 days. Cymoxanil + Mancozeb @ 2g/litre as alternating spray. Apply when weather is dry — rain washes off fungicide.
Potato_Late_blight.organic_alternative: Copper hydroxide (3g/litre) spray as preventive measure. Bicarbonate of soda solution (5g/litre) can slow spread. Harvest tubers early if condition deteriorates rapidly.
Potato_Late_blight.farmer_tips:
1. Never save tubers from a blight-infected crop for next season's seed.
2. Space plants 60-75cm apart for better airflow.
3. Grow on ridges to improve drainage away from tubers.
4. Monitor weather forecasts — warm humid weather (above 10°C with >90% humidity) triggers blight.
5. Plant resistant varieties such as Kufri Jyoti or Kufri Bahar.

Potato_healthy.symptoms: Plants show uniform green foliage with strong stems. Leaves are fully expanded without spots or wilting.
Potato_healthy.prevention: Maintain soil nutrients and irrigation balance.
Potato_healthy.advice: Maintain consistent irrigation and monitor weekly for any early pest signs.
Potato_healthy.immediate_action: No immediate action needed. Your potato crop is in excellent condition.
Potato_healthy.organic_alternative: Apply compost or FYM (farmyard manure) 20 tonnes/hectare before planting. Use Trichoderma-enriched compost for soil health.
Potato_healthy.farmer_tips:
1. Irrigate every 7-10 days — avoid waterlogging.
2. Earth up (hill soil) around plants when they are 15-20cm tall.
3. Apply potassium-rich fertilizer to strengthen tuber development.
4. Scout for aphids weekly — they spread potato viruses.
5. Remove and destroy any plant showing wilting or abnormal coloration immediately.

Rice_Brownspot.symptoms: Small dark brown oval to circular spots on leaves with yellowish halo. Grains may also show dark spots reducing grain quality and market value.
Rice_Brownspot.treatment: Spray Carbendazim 50 WP or Mancozeb 75 WP.
Rice_Brownspot.prevention: Use certified seeds. Balance nitrogen and potassium fertilizers. Avoid excessive nitrogen.
Rice_Brownspot.advice: Brown spot is strongly associated with nutrient deficiency, especially silicon and potassium. Address soil nutrition alongside fungicide treatment.
Rice_Brownspot.immediate_action: Apply fungicide spray within 48 hours of noticing spots. Also apply potassium fertilizer as soil nutrition deficiencies make plants more susceptible.
Rice_Brownspot.chemical_treatment: Carbendazim 50 WP @ 1g/litre or Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5g/litre, 2-3 sprays at 10-day intervals. Tricyclazole 75 WP @ 0.6g/litre for severe cases.
Rice_Brownspot.organic_alternative: Spray neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) solution. Silica-rich amendments (rice husk ash) improve plant resistance. Apply compost enriched with Trichoderma viride.
Rice_Brownspot.farmer_tips:
1. Test soil before planting and correct potassium and silicon deficiencies.
2. Avoid excessive nitrogen (urea) application — it worsens brown spot.
3. Use certified seeds treated with Thiram or Carbendazim before sowing.
4. Maintain proper water level in paddy fields — do not allow water stress.
5. Grow resistant varieties recommended for your region.

Rice_Bacterialblight.symptoms: Leaf tips and edges turn yellow then brown and dry. Water-soaked lesions spread downward along leaf margins. Bacterial ooze visible on cut stems in the morning.
Rice_Bacterialblight.treatment: Spray Streptocycline 90 SP @ 0.5g/litre combined with Copper fungicide.
Rice_Bacterialblight.prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Do not flood field from infected areas. Use resistant varieties.
Rice_Bacterialblight.advice: Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB) is one of the most destructive rice diseases. It spreads through irrigation water, rain, and insects.
Rice_Bacterialblight.immediate_action: Drain excess water from the field. Do not irrigate from infected area. Apply bactericide immediately. Avoid applying nitrogen fertilizer until disease is under control.
Rice_Bacterialblight.chemical_treatment: Streptocycline 90 SP @ 0.5g/litre + Copper Oxychloride 50 WP @ 3g/litre. Spray 2-3 times at 10-day intervals. Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer during treatment.
Rice_Bacterialblight.organic_alternative: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens bio-pesticide (10g/litre). Avoid flooding from upstream infected fields. Apply potassium fertilizer to strengthen plant cell walls.
Rice_Bacterialblight.farmer_tips:
1. Do NOT irrigate from fields where BLB is present — it spreads in water.
2. Avoid excess nitrogen (urea) application during and after disease period.
3. Use disease-free seeds — untreated seeds can carry the bacteria.
4. Remove and burn infected plant material — do not incorporate into soil.
5. Plant BLB-resistant varieties like IR-64, Swarna Sub-1, or region-recommended varieties.

Rice_Healthy.symptoms: Plants show erect green leaves with strong tillers. No discoloration, spots, or wilting observed.
Rice_Healthy.prevention: Maintain proper irrigation and balanced fertilization.
Rice_Healthy.advice: Maintain consistent irrigation and monitor weekly for any early pest signs.
Rice_Healthy.immediate_action: No immediate action needed. Your rice crop looks healthy.
Rice_Healthy.organic_alternative: Apply compost at 5 tonnes/hectare. Use Azospirillum + Phosphobacteria bio-fertilizers to reduce chemical fertilizer dependency.
Rice_Healthy.farmer_tips:
1. Maintain 5-7cm water level in paddy fields during vegetative stage.
2. Apply balanced NPK at recommended rates for your soil type.
3. Scout for stem borers and leaf folders weekly — early detection saves yield.
4. Do not allow water stress during flowering — it reduces grain filling.
5. Drain field 1-2 weeks before harvest for easy machine harvesting.

Wheat_Brown_rust.symptoms: Small round to oval brown-orange pustules scattered on upper leaf surfaces. Infected leaves die early reducing grain filling and yield.
Wheat_Brown_rust.prevention: Grow resistant wheat varieties. Early sowing before peak rust season reduces risk.
Wheat_Brown_rust.advice: Rust spreads by wind — once spotted in your region, act fast. A 3-week delay can result in 30-50% yield loss.
Wheat_Brown_rust.immediate_action: Apply fungicide spray within 24-48 hours of first pustule detection. Scout neighboring fields — rust spreads rapidly by wind.
Wheat_Brown_rust.chemical_treatment: Propiconazole 25 EC @ 1ml/litre, 1-2 sprays at 14-day intervals. Hexaconazole 5 EC @ 1.5ml/litre as alternative. Tebuconazole 250 EC @ 1ml/litre for severe infections.
Wheat_Brown_rust.organic_alternative: Sulfur dust (20kg/hectare) applied early can slow rust development. Neem oil spray (5ml/litre) may suppress pustule formation. Focus on planting resistant varieties for long-term solution.
Wheat_Brown_rust.farmer_tips:
1. Plant rust-resistant varieties such as HD 2967, GW 496, or region-approved varieties.
2. Early sowing (October-November) avoids peak rust season.
3. Apply balanced nitrogen — excess nitrogen increases rust severity.
4. Report rust outbreaks to local agricultural department — they may issue regional advisories.
5. Save seeds only from rust-free plots for next season.

Wheat_Yellow_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow pustules arranged in striking stripe patterns along leaf veins. In severe cases entire leaves turn yellow and die. Yield losses can exceed 50%.
Wheat_Yellow_rust.prevention: Early sowing. Use of resistant varieties. Remove infected volunteer plants before the season.
Wheat_Yellow_rust.advice: Yellow rust thrives in cool moist weather (10-15°C). It is the most damaging wheat rust. A single infected plant can spread disease to an entire region via wind-blown spores.
Wheat_Yellow_rust.immediate_action: URGENT: Spray systemic fungicide immediately. Yellow rust spreads faster than brown rust — one week's delay can cause 30-50% yield loss. Alert fellow farmers in your area.
Wheat_Yellow_rust.chemical_treatment: Tebuconazole 250 EC @ 1ml/litre spray, repeat in 14 days if needed. Propiconazole 25 EC @ 1ml/litre as alternative. Triadimefon 25 WP @ 1g/litre for systemic control.
Wheat_Yellow_rust.organic_alternative: Sulfur 80 WP (3g/litre) spray may reduce pustule development. Focus on resistant variety selection for ongoing protection. Biocontrol with Bacillus subtilis provides some suppression.
Wheat_Yellow_rust.farmer_tips:
1. Monitor wheat fields from December onwards — yellow rust appears in cool humid weather.
2. Check flag leaf (topmost leaf) — infection here causes maximum yield loss.
3. Plant resistant varieties: WH-1105, PBW-550, or varieties recommended by your state.
4. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer — it makes plants more susceptible.
5. Never allow infected wheat to mature and flower — it releases spores that spread to next season.

Wheat_Healthy.symptoms: Crop shows uniform green growth with erect tillers. Leaves are free of any spots, pustules, or discoloration.
Wheat_Healthy.prevention: Balanced fertilization and regular field monitoring.
Wheat_Healthy.advice: Maintain consistent irrigation and monitor weekly for any early pest signs.
Wheat_Healthy.immediate_action: No immediate action required. Maintain your current crop management practices.
Wheat_Healthy.chemical_treatment: No chemical treatment needed at this stage.
Wheat_Healthy.organic_alternative: Apply compost or well-rotted FYM before sowing. Use phosphate solubilizing bacteria biofertilizer for better root development.
Wheat_Healthy.farmer_tips:
1. Apply first irrigation at 20-25 days after sowing (Crown Root Initiation stage).
2. Apply balanced NPK — phosphorus is critical for root and grain development.
3. Scout weekly for aphids, stem borers, and rust pustules.
4. Avoid late-season lodging — stake or mound soil around weak tillers.
5. Harvest at proper maturity (grain moisture 12-14%) for best quality.

Pepper_bell_Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked dark spots on leaves and pepper fruits. Spots enlarge with yellow margins. Infected fruits develop scabby lesions reducing market value.
Pepper_bell_Bacterial_spot.prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation and use healthy disease-free seedlings.
Pepper_bell_Bacterial_spot.advice: Practice 2-3 year crop rotation. Manage irrigation to reduce humidity around foliage. Balance fertilizer applications.
Pepper_bell_Bacterial_spot.immediate_action: Switch to drip irrigation immediately — overhead watering spreads bacteria. Apply copper-based bactericide the same day. Remove heavily infected fruits.
Pepper_bell_Bacterial_spot.chemical_treatment: Copper Oxychloride 50 WP @ 3g/litre weekly spray. Streptocycline @ 0.5g/litre combined with copper fungicide provides better control. Kasugamycin 3 SL @ 2ml/litre as alternative bactericide.
Pepper_bell_Bacterial_spot.organic_alternative: Spray diluted neem oil with copper soap solution (3ml neem oil + 2g copper soap/litre). Hot water seed treatment (52°C for 30 minutes) to eliminate seed-borne bacteria. Use biocontrol agent Bacillus subtilis (0.5%).
Pepper_bell_Bacterial_spot.farmer_tips:
1. Buy seeds from certified disease-free nurseries only.
2. Use drip irrigation — never overhead sprinklers for pepper.
3. Space plants 45-60cm apart for good airflow between plants.
4. Sanitize all pruning tools with 10% bleach solution before each plant.
5. Avoid working in the field when foliage is wet — you spread bacteria on your hands and clothes.
